hook.text: An American in Japan bows too deep. A European in India eats with the wrong hand. Small surprises pile into exhaustion.

buildup.text: Culture shock is sustained surprise: every social norm you took for granted becomes a puzzle to solve.

discovery.text: Kalervo Oberg identified four stages: honeymoon, frustration, adjustment, and adaptation.

twist.text: Reverse culture shock is often worse. Returning home, you're surprised by norms you once found obvious.

climax.text: People who adapt well to culture shock show higher cognitive flexibility in tests years later.

punchline.text: Culture shock is your brain rebuilding normal from scratch.

quiz.question: Who identified the four stages of culture shock?
